titulo: Closing the loop: failure log and observability
lead: What isn't observed isn't cultivated. This lesson follows a clinic front-desk agent from its first error to supervised autonomy, and shows the minimum you need to record to replace "I think it got better" with "it improved from 88% to 95%".
objetivo: record each run with the minimum set of fields and turn a real error into a new rule, comparing the result before and after.

aprende.t: How an error becomes a permanent rule
Finding the error pattern worth fixing first

hero_alt: Clinic receptionist checks the appointment schedule on the screen next to an open notebook.

secoes.titulo: The clinic case, in six stages
secoes.sub: Scroll to follow along. The numbers are from the case described in the project.

nos.detalhe: Doctors and specialties, each doctor's hours, procedures and duration, clinic rules, and access to the schedule. The agent only suggests; the receptionist approves each appointment.

The agent books 7:30 PM with a doctor who doesn't see patients after 6 PM. The schedule showed "free," but a free schedule slot is not an available doctor. The failure is logged with date, decision, result, and root cause.

nos.sub: In the environment, not in the conversation
nos.detalhe: "Before suggesting, check the schedule AND the doctor's working hours. Outside working hours, never, even if the schedule shows free." Takes effect from the next run onward.
Of the next 20 interactions, 18 were correct. The 2 failures become two more rules: the procedure's duration must fit in the time slot, and 15 minutes between appointments.
40 interactions in two weeks: 20/20 in each, zero corrections from the receptionist, response time from 4 minutes to 45 seconds.

nos.sub: Runs on its own; a human reviews exceptions
nos.detalhe: With the history, the agent starts confirming on its own. The human gets a daily report and reviews only what the agent flagged as an exception: cutoff time, new patient, long procedure.

rolagem_fim.texto: Rules: from 5 generic ones to 14 born from real failures. 320 runs logged, 7 failures documented, 97.8% accuracy, version v1.0 → v1.4. The model is the same as on day one; if the clinic switches models, the garden stays.

secoes.sub: What observability shows (project example, 100 runs in each version).

texto: Three error patterns: outside the professional's hours (5), time slot too short for the procedure (4), and an ambiguous reply about cancellation (3).
Each pattern produced a new rule: four rules modified.
Patterns 1 and 2 disappeared. Pattern 3 dropped from 3 to 1 occurrence.
A new pattern showed up: two simultaneous procedures requesting the same exam room. The cycle goes on.

exemplo.texto: From 88% to 95% with rules and fixes. Nobody switched the model: they looked at the data and adjusted the environment.

texto: Compare versions on the same scenarios. Find patterns ("70% of errors are long procedures"). Measure the cost of an error ("each rescheduling costs R$ 150"). Decide where to invest first.

secoes.sub: Start with the three fields. The full version comes when the volume calls for it.

exercicios.texto: For the function you chose, log every run in EXECUCOES.md with the three minimum fields.
exercicios.pronto: the file has at least 10 rows and you can state the week's accuracy rate (e.g., 8 out of 10).

exercicios.titulo: 2 · A rule born from an error
exercicios.texto: Take the failure that repeated most during the week and fill in the "from failure to rule" template. Put the rule in the file and bump the version.
exercicios.pronto: the rule is written in the agent's file, the version went up (v1.0 → v1.1), and the next runs are being counted so you can compare.

perguntas.p: The calendar showed the time slot as free and the agent booked outside the doctor's working hours. What was the root cause?
opcoes: The calendar wasn't being cross-checked against the doctor's working hours: a missing rule
perguntas.explica: A free calendar slot is not an available doctor. The fix was a permanent rule in the environment, not a new model.

perguntas.p: What is the minimum viable observability?
opcoes: What was asked, what was delivered, and whether it worked
perguntas.explica: Three fields are enough to calculate accuracy and close the first cycle. More fields come in when the volume calls for it.

perguntas.p: In v1.1 a new error pattern appeared (exam room conflict). That means that...
opcoes: v1.1 got worse and should be rolled back
the cycle is working: new pattern, new rule
the agent has reached the limit
perguntas.explica: The old patterns are gone and the rate went up from 88% to 95%. New patterns show up when the old ones get out of the way.

perguntas.p: After 2 months, what does the clinic have that a competitor can't copy by hiring the same model?
opcoes: The 14 rules born from failures, the history, and the logs
perguntas.explica: The garden belongs to the clinic. If it switches models, the garden stays; whoever copies the model starts from zero.

itens.texto: A log with the root cause, the smallest fix, the rule in the file, and a new version.
Same scenarios, before and after: 88% → 95% without changing the model.
Request, delivery, did it work. That already closes the first cycle.
